texts.facts: The case of the petitioner: 4. The petitioner is a registered manufacturer under Excise Act and GST Act, carrying on the business in trading of tobacco under the name, "hans chhap tobacco". The Learned Judge, held that Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (FSS Act) and Cigarette and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (herein after referred as "COTPA") occupy different fields (i.e) FSS Act applies to food industry, while COTPA applies to tobacco industry. Hence, declared that the Notification issued by the Food Safety Department is clear abuse of the power. Since on the date of seizure and as well as on the date of complaint, there was stay of the Notification issued by the Governmet of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis NCT, Delhi, the complaint laid against the petitioner for manufacturing and distributing their product is not sustainable.
texts.arguments: Without proper appreciation and understanding of the provision of law, the complaint been registered under the premises that tobacco is a food product and the petitioner has manufactured unsafe food product. Unless tobacco is mixed in a food product, the petitioner cannot be implicated for manufacturing unsafe food. In fact, they are duly registered under the GST Act and Excise Act, paying tax for their product, which is primarily tobacco and covered under COTPA and not under FSS Act. The liquor company which manufactures and sell in the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis territory which permits such manufacturering and sale, cannot be prosecuted for the mere presence of their product in the States where there is a prohibition. While sale of chewable tobacco is banned in Tamilnadu and the sample drawn declared as unsafe by the lab, the petitioner's company is liable to be proscuted. The petitioner being the manufacturer of the product prohibited for sale in Tamilnadu, bound to explain how their product found way to Tamilnadu.
